Our family went from a thermal coffee brewer to a Keurig.  I was a little skeptical at first, but the freshness and taste of each cup even beat the thermal.  As good as it tastes, I'm a heavy coffee consumer and buying the individual Kcups quickly became taxing on the wallet.  Doing a little searching I found these filters and decided to give them a try.  Simply amazing.  It's not as convenient (have to clean them out) as a Kcup but the money I am saving far outweighs the inconvenience.  The family gets to have the variety of their Kcups and I use these with my regular coffee.  Win-win.  Be sure to use a larger ground for these or you will get a little dust in the coffee.  We have also found they work great for loose tea.

I cannot get these pods to make anything except a very weak cup of coffee.  My Keurig has 4 size setttings and a "strong" setting.  Even at the smallest size, and the "strong" setting activated, and the POD completely filled with the coffee grinds of a dark roast, the coffee still comes out weak.  I believe these pods are too porous.  They allow for the drainage of liquid on all sides of the Pod; whereas a disposable pod would only release the coffee from the bottom.  I'm guessing that this causes water to leave the pod before it has pulled enough flavor from the grinds.
